title: Stop the range for from copying
summary: Every element is being copied. Take it by const auto&, and by auto& where it is written.

turns.user: total_bytes gets weirdly slow around 100k rows. it only adds numbers up

assistant.body: Here's the cost: for (auto record : records) copies every element. Record holds a std::string, so each turn of the loop allocates. Binding a reference makes the copy go away.

turns.user: oh there is also normalize below it, that one assigns to record.tag. same fix?

assistant.body: Not quite. That one wants auto& with no const. The reference is what avoids the copy and the const is what forbids the write, and they are separate choices. As it stands normalize edits a copy, so nothing reaches the vector.
